problem: Existing EQA/VQA datasets mostly contain purely verbal questions posed from a single perspective (speaker or observer). They do not cover multimodal referring expressions, where a human asks questions using both speech and non-verbal cues (gaze, pointing), or the interchangeable speaker/observer/neutral perspectives found in real interactions.
motivation: EQA needs language understanding, perception, navigation, memory and reasoning, and data is central to training and evaluating such agents. In real human–robot interaction people point, look, and describe objects from different viewpoints (e.g., 'right of the cup' from the speaker is 'left' for the observer). Datasets lacking these multimodal and multi-perspective cues are argued to hinder QA model development.
key_idea: Build a multimodal, multi-perspective EQA dataset with eight question-answering tasks. Frames come from several camera views and include human avatars with gaze and pointing gestures, aggregated and relabeled from EmbodiedQA, R2R/Matterport3D and ALFRED. Off-the-shelf vision-language models are benchmarked on it.
insight: The benchmark shows that standard single-context VL models (Dual-Encoder ViT+BERT, CLIP, ViLT) handle binary or grounding-style tasks reasonably well, e.g. RG ~89–90% and POG 82.7–87.4%. All three fail at object counting under spatial relations (OC 12.3–13.1%), so relational counting is the clear open challenge. ViLT's large lead on existence prediction (91.5 vs ~55) and perspective grounding (81.2 vs ~67) suggests early cross-modal fusion helps on these tasks, but the paper offers no ablation or analysis to confirm why. Readers should also note that the task taxonomy, the four human-cue scenarios and the evaluated models closely mirror EQA-MX / CAESAR (Islam et al.), which this paper does not cite.
method: Eight EQA tasks: Existence Prediction (EP), Object Grounding (OG), Perspective-aware Object Grounding (POG), Object Counting (OC), Object Attribute Query (OAQ), Object Attribute Compare (OAC), Perspective Grounding (PG) and Relation Grounding (RG); questions combine verbal utterances with non-verbal gestures and specify speaker/observer/neutral perspective.
Data aggregation/relabeling: combines, filters and re-annotates data from EmbodiedQA (FAIR), Matterport3D R2R and ALFRED (AI2-THOR) to produce task-specific QA data.

Scenario generation: four scenarios per visual scene (no human, human gaze, human pointing, gaze + pointing); pointing gestures are generated procedurally via inverse kinematics in Unity; camera viewpoints and object placements are varied for generalization.

Multi-view frames: each sample has frames from the agent's (egocentric) view, an external (exocentric) view and a top-down view, plus perspective annotations and per-task questions/answers; data is split into train/validation/test (Table 2, units unstated).

Baseline evaluation: Dual-Encoder (shared ViT per view + BERT for text, fused into a task representation), CLIP (each view paired with the question, multiple representations fused), and ViLT (described as using ResNet-101 visual features plus word embeddings); per-task answer accuracy is reported.
Release: data, training environment and experiments are packaged as a Singularity container built from a Docker image.

setting.backbone: Evaluated off-the-shelf VL models: Dual-Encoder (ViT + BERT), CLIP, ViLT; no new model proposed
setting.training_data: The paper's own dataset (train split per Table 2: e.g. 106 per task for EP/OG/POG/OC/OAQ, 28 OAC, 78 PG, 34 RG; units not stated, likely thousands), built by relabeling EmbodiedQA, R2R/Matterport3D and ALFRED data plus Unity-generated gaze/pointing scenarios
setting.observation: static RGB frames from multiple views (agent egocentric, external/exocentric, top-down) + natural-language question with non-verbal human cues
setting.action_space: none (static-frame QA; no navigation actions evaluated)
setting.simulator: Unity-based scene generation (inverse kinematics for gestures); source data from House3D/AI2-THOR (EmbodiedQA, ALFRED) and Matterport3D (R2R)
setting.privileged: none (no navigation; QA from provided frames)

numbers_note: Table 4 reports per-task answer accuracy (%) for three baseline VL models on the paper's own dataset; the paper does not state whether this is the validation or evaluation split (recorded as 'test'). Figure 4 only re-plots Table 4. There are no standard navigation benchmarks, no navigation metrics and no proposed model. Table 2 dataset sizes have no units.
results: On the new dataset, the three VL baselines perform similarly overall. ViLT is best on EP (91.5), POG (87.4) and PG (81.2); CLIP is best on OG (65.4), OAQ (74.3), OAC (70.5) and RG (89.9). Object counting is very poor for all models (12.3–13.1%), which the author identifies as the key open challenge. No proposed method is compared against these baselines.
limitations: No new model or navigation agent is evaluated; the tasks are static-frame QA, so the 'embodied' and navigation aspects are not actually tested. The introduction's claim of a new multimodal training model is not delivered.

Dataset construction is under-specified: Table 2 sizes lack units, the source-data descriptions are partly inaccurate (e.g., EmbodiedQA described as AI2-THOR/House3D ~5,000 questions), and it is unclear which split Table 4 reports.

The task taxonomy (EP/OG/POG/OC/OAQ/OAC/PG/RG), the four gaze/pointing scenarios with Unity inverse kinematics, and the Dual-Encoder/CLIP/ViLT baselines closely mirror EQA-MX / CAESAR (Islam et al.), which is not cited, so novelty is unclear. Model descriptions also contain errors (ViLT is described with ResNet-101 and cited to ViT-NET).
